subject: Model window, throughput & ramp plan for Celerus onboarding
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@celerus.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Josef Klein <jk@celerus.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding data + context windows for inference planning

Hi Jasmine / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I’m sending a quick snapshot of our expected traffic and functional constraints so you can start sizing models and recommending a shortlist. Attached: celerus_initial_traffic.csv (daily burst + steady-state).

A few clarifications from our side:
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support summarization and agent assist. Typical convo length: 6-12 turns, average context size ~1.2k tokens, but we have a 5% tail that needs ~6k tokens (full transcript + metadata).
- Peak Q1 ramp: target go-live Jan 15; expected 90-day ramp to 20k daily active users; token mix weighted toward short responses but with occasional long retrospects.
- Latency SLO: 800ms p95 for short-context assist; we can tolerate 2s p95 on the long transcript summarize path.

Can you confirm what model family you recommend for: (A) low-latency agent assist, (B) high-context summarization, and (C) a single fall-back model for graceful degradation? Also need a rough 6-month token burn estimate to FY planning.

Cheers,
Alicia
Director of Product
Celerus AI

---
Attachment: celerus_initial_traffic.csv (type: text/csv, 28KB)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@celerus.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding data + context windows for inference planning

Hi Alicia — thanks for the file, that helps a lot. I looped in Monica (solutions) and Ben (account) to align technical and commercial constraints. I’ve attached a short note with a candidate model shortlist and rationale. Key assumptions up front:
- We’ll treat the 6k-token tail as an explicit "long-context" route that can be routed to a high-memory model variant with looser latency SLOs.
- For agent assist we prioritize throughput; we'll evaluate 8k and 16k variants for cost vs. latency.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Monica to validate quantify token breakdown and provide a 6-month token burn estimate (conservative / expected / optimistic).
2) Schedule a 60-min kickoff to lock routing policy (latency vs cost) and canary timeline.
3) Ben to confirm commercial trigger dates and any committed capacity thresholds.

Draft attached: model_shortlist_notes.pdf (shortlist: two low-latency candidates, two high-context candidates, plus a 4-bit quantized fall-back). Please review and tell us if you have constraints around on-prem / private deployment for the long-context transcripts.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the details, Alicia and Jasmine. I dug into the CSV and started a conservative token model. High-level results below and attached my workbook with the line-by-line assumptions.

Summary (conservative / expected / optimistic for 6 months):
- Total prompt tokens: 42M / 29M / 18M
- Total completion tokens: 56M / 38M / 22M
- Long-context (6k tokens) estimate: 3.2M prompt tokens in conservative case (these are expensive due to full attention).

Model shortlist (technical rationale):
- Low-latency assist: FP16 tuned family A (8k context variant) — best p95 latency at load and good cost envelope.
- High-context summarize: 32k/context family B (memory-optimized, mixed-precision) — recommended for the 6k tail to avoid truncation and preserve accuracy.
- Fallback: quantized 4-bit variant of family A for burst capacity and cost control; route only when Dedicated pool saturates.

Ops guidance:
- Start with a Dedicated pool sized for expected Q1 steady-state (we can size for 1.5x expected to handle buffer), enable burst to hosted for overflow.
- Prefix caching for short-turn assistant (many prompts repeat); implement evaluation hooks to track quality delta if we switch quantized variants.

Attachment: celerus_onboarding_token_estimates.xlsx (type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 96KB)

Let me know if you want a quick call to walk the sheet — I can run alternate scenarios (faster ramp, heavier tail).

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
